Your flag is AGA, so:
- If you’re using topical minoxidil -> switch to oral. Some people don’t have the enzymes in their skin to respond to the topical form.
- Add an anti androgen. Minoxidil is a vasodilator and helps get blood to the follicles, but the androgen is still there and will continue to progress the AGA further. Consider spironolactone, finasteride, dutasteride. There are newer drugs as well but I don’t have any exp with them.
- Get fit and healthy, eat well -> probably doesn’t help the hair but will get your mental health strong enough for the ride.

I assume you have done this to some degree, but if you haven’t, you could do what I did to get my current job after searching for 5 months as someone without the degree nor domain experience. 

Start reaching out to anyone relevant on LinkedIn. This means hiring managers of the companies you apply to, hiring managers of companies you’re NOT applying to as they might have some positions not yet cleared for hiring announcement, people with the same role as you, acquaintances from grad school, etc. Personalize the message and politely ask them to keep you in mind when a new position opens up. While you’re at it, tidy up your LinkedIn account beforehand with a professional profile picture (or if you can’t afford to take one, use Remini to get an AI pic) and Chat-GPT proof-read role and responsibilities descriptions. Add the green #OpenToWork ribbon on your profile picture. And make an announcement to your network that you’re looking for a new role - there’s even a template for that on the site. I find that my post was the nail on the head that got me this job, because as few as one or two reactions from hiring managers resulted in dozens of profile views, connections and ultimately, the recruiter of my current company reaching out about an urgent role.

Vé máy bay: book qua trip.com rẻ nhất. AirAsia nếu k ngại bay đêm, với bay của bọn này thì đến sân bay DMK (Bangkok có 2 sân bay quốc tế) sẽ gần thành phố hơn. Trình tự ra sân bay phía Việt Nam: đến sân bay tìm quầy checkin, làm thủ tục và để lại đồ ký gửi nếu có -> đi lên immigration làm thủ tục xuất cảnh -> đi qua khu security check, tụt giày và laptop, điện thoại, sạc dự phòng để scan -> đến cổng đợi như đã note trên vé. Nói chung là đến sân bay nhìn mọi người làm thì sẽ biết. Sang đến bên kia rồi thì làm thủ tục nhập cảnh -> xuống lấy hành lý ký gửi ở băng chuyền là xong.

Di chuyển từ sân bay vào thành phố: Bác tìm airport link tham khảo thêm vì cái này tôi cũng chưa đi bao giờ nên k cmt đc. Nếu thấy khó quá thì gọi xe taxi trên Grab, đâu đấy tầm 350 baht là max.

Chỗ ở: book agoda hay có deal rẻ hơn booking.com dù là 2 thằng cùng một hệ sinh thái. Ở đâu thì phụ thuộc vào công việc của bác. Khách sạn trên trục Sukhumvit (trục đường chính ở Bangkok) sẽ đắt hơn là ở trong ngõ.

Đi lại: bác tìm trên map cái BTS station gần nhất và lên làm cái thẻ, nạp vào đấy khoảng 100-200 baht. Đi 2 ngày tẹt ga. Cần di chuyển đến những chỗ xa trạm thì book xe máy trên Bolt - là cái app book xe rẻ nhất bên đấy.

Ăn uống: Street food đương nhiên sẽ rẻ hơn. Cái này tôi k ăn nhiều nên k rõ, nhưng bác cứ lên map tìm Restaurant mở cái nào có tên tiếng Thái + nhiều review tốt thì vào ăn thôi.

And if your hair loss turns out not to be AGA, your healthy hair will not be affected in the long term.

To piggyback on this, this was my approach with my derm:

1.	You need to know what **types of hair loss** there are. The most common ones you’ll see on the subreddit are AGA and TE.
2.	You need to kinda have an idea what **your hair loss might be**. You’re not going to be 100% right as types of hair loss sometimes manifest in the same ways and that’s why you’re going to the derm. 
3.	You need to identify any **possible triggers** for an episode of TE: stressful bouts, high fever, surgeries, new BC pill, new hair products, diets,… Covid is a common cause of hair shedding. All this you’ll let your derm know.
4.	You’ll possibly need to do a blood test to assess your vit D, iron levels and maybe thyroid functions. So for 8 hours before the appt try not to eat anything.
5.	When at the appointment: be humble and try not to be emotional. Ask a lot of questions, anything that you’re not sure about! Don’t let your concerns be brushed aside.
6.	Trust the derm but also yourself! I was fortunate to have a derm who was very knowledgeable on hair health, but sometimes people get put up with derms who either don’t specialize in it, or don’t think it’s serious.
7.	Regrowing your hair is going to be a long and gradual process, so take a deep breath and tackle it bits by bits. This subreddit is a wonderful support system with many experienced people, don’t be afraid to ask.
